thought_title: Truly born, truly crucified, truly raised

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Κωφώθητε οὖν, ὅταν ὑμῖν χωρὶς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ λαλῇ τις, τοῦ ἐκ γένους Δαυείδ, τοῦ ἐκ Μαρίας, ὃς ἀληθῶς ἐγεννήθη, ἔφαγέν τε καὶ ἔπιεν, ἀληθῶς ἐδιώχθη ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτον, ἀληθῶς ἐσταυρώθη καὶ ἀπέθανεν, βλεπόντων τῶν ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων καὶ ὑποχθονίων. [2] ὃς καὶ ἀληθῶς ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ νεκρῶν. ἐγείραντος αὐτὸν τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ, κατὰ τὸ ὁμοίωμα ὃς καὶ ἡμᾶς τοὺς πιστεύοντας αὐτῷ οὕτως ἐγερεῖ ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, οὗ χωρὶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν ζῆν οὐκ ἔχομεν.
pass_a_gloss: Be deaf, then, whenever anyone speaks to you apart from Jesus Christ, who was of the family of David, who was of Mary, who was truly born, both ate and drank, was truly persecuted under Pontius Pilate, was truly crucified and died, while beings in heaven, on earth, and under the earth were watching; who was also truly raised from the dead, his Father having raised him; according to the likeness of this, his Father will likewise raise us also who believe in him, in Christ Jesus, apart from whom we do not have the true living.
pass_b_english: Go deaf, then, when anyone speaks to you apart from Jesus Christ, of David's line, of Mary, who was truly born, who ate and drank, was truly hounded under Pontius Pilate, was truly crucified and died, while those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth looked on (Philippians 2:10); who was also truly raised from the dead.
His Father raised him. And in just that way his Father will raise us too, we who believe in him (2 Corinthians 4:14), in Christ Jesus. Without him we have no true life.

choices.why: Aorist passive imperative: become deaf, a sharp command; the game draft's 'Go deaf' keeps the bite.
The repeated adverb is the anti-docetic hammer; each instance kept in place.
διώκω = pursue, persecute; 'hounded' keeps the pursuit sense in plain English (owner's game draft).

choices.term: βλεπόντων τῶν ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων καὶ ὑποχθονίων
choices.english: while those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth looked on
choices.why: Genitive absolute with personal plurals (beings watching). Refines the game draft's 'heaven, earth, and the world below' to keep beings as the watchers and the Philippians 2:10 triad.
rejected: while heaven, earth, and the world below looked on (game draft; turns watchers into places)

choices.english: in just that way his Father will raise us too
choices.why: ὁμοίωμα + οὕτως: our resurrection follows the pattern of his.

anf_compare.notes: Modernized ANF span matches in sense; it stops at 'his Father raising him'; Greek sections continue through 9.2.

bible_refs.note: Triad ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων καὶ καταχθονίων (Ignatius: ὑποχθονίων). Allusion.
ὁ ἐγείρας τὸν κύριον Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἡμᾶς σὺν Ἰησοῦ ἐγερεῖ. Allusion. Lake marks 1 Corinthians 15:12 ff.; recorded in notes.

notes: Span = Trallians 9.1–2 (both sections). Shared English across the five Trallians 9 ids.
Lake apparatus at 9.2: κατὰ τὸ ὁμοίωμα ὃς καί G; L 'qui et secundum similitudinem'; SA perhaps imply ὡς καί. The relative ὃς is anacoluthic; translated for sense (his Father will raise us likewise).
Lake's margin marks I Cor 15:12 ff. at 9.2 (resurrection argument); wording is closer to 2 Corinthians 4:14 (ὁ ἐγείρας … καὶ ἡμᾶς … ἐγερεῖ), which is tagged inline.
τὸ ἀληθινὸν ζῆν: articular infinitive, 'true living/life'.
Owner game draft kept for 9.1 except the watchers clause (see choices).

review.notes: Checked paragraph [1] (Trallians 9.1–2). Κωφώθητε οὖν, ὅταν ὑμῖν χωρὶς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ λαλῇ τις matches A “Be deaf, then, whenever anyone speaks to you apart from Jesus Christ” and B “Go deaf, then, when anyone speaks to you apart from Jesus Christ.” Fourfold ἀληθῶς kept: ἀληθῶς ἐγεννήθη, ἔφαγέν τε καὶ ἔπιεν, ἀληθῶς ἐδιώχθη… ἀληθῶς ἐσταυρώθη καὶ ἀπέθανεν… ἀληθῶς ἠγέρθη = A “truly born, both ate and drank… truly persecuted… truly crucified and died… truly raised” and B “truly born, who ate and drank… truly hounded… truly crucified and died… truly raised.” Watchers βλεπόντων τῶν ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων καὶ ὑποχθονίων stay persons in both. Agency: ἐγείραντος αὐτὸν τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ… ἐγερεῖ ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ = A “his Father having raised him… his Father will likewise raise us” and B “His Father raised him… his Father will raise us too.” Negation οὗ χωρὶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν ζῆν οὐκ ἔχομεν = A “apart from whom we do not have the true living” and B “Without him we have no true life.” Inline (Philippians 2:10) and (2 Corinthians 4:14) identify the triad and raising allusions given in the supplied notes. Title names the anti-docetic thought.

Source: Ignatius Trallians 9 (Lake 1912 Loeb). Paragraph 1 contains two sentences: [1] Κωφώθητε οὖν...ἀπέθανεν, βλεπόντων τῶν ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων καὶ ὑποχθονίων. [2] ὃς καὶ ἀληθῶς ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ νεκρῶν...οὐκ ἔχομεν. Pass A gloss renders all clauses: 'Be deaf...apart from Jesus Christ...who was of the family of David, who was of Mary, who was truly born, both ate and drank, was truly persecuted under Pontius Pilate, was truly crucified and died, while beings in heaven, on earth, and under the earth were watching; who was also truly raised from the dead, his Father having raised him; according to the likeness of this, his Father will likewise raise us also who believe in him, in Christ Jesus, apart from whom we do not have the true living.' Pass B English splits into two strings: ['Go deaf, then, when anyone speaks to you apart from Jesus Christ, of David's line, of Mary, who was truly born, who ate and drank, was truly hounded under Pontius Pilate, was truly crucified and died, while those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth looked on (Philippians 2:10); who was also truly raised from the dead.', 'His Father raised him. And in just that way his Father will raise us too, we who believe in him (2 Corinthians 4:14), in Christ Jesus. Without him we have no true life.']. All Greek clauses are accounted for: imperative κωφώθητε (Go deaf/Be deaf), temporal clause ὅταν...λαλῇ, appositives τοῦ ἐκ γένους Δαυείδ, τοῦ ἐκ Μαρίας, series of ἀληθῶς participles (ἐγεννήθη, ἔφαγεν τε καὶ ἔπιεν, ἐδιώχθη, ἐσταυρώθη, ἀπέθανεν), genitive absolute βλεπόντων..., second sentence ὃς καὶ ἀληθῶς ἠγέρθη..., participial clause ἐγείραντος αὐτὸν τοῦ πατρός αὐτοῦ, comparative clause κατὰ τὸ ὁμοίωμα ὃς καί..., final clause οὗ χωρὶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν ζῆν οὐκ ἔχομεν. Negation: οὖν (therefore) preserved in Pass A 'then', οὐκ ἔχομεν rendered 'we do not have' (Pass A) and 'Without him we have no' (Pass B). Agency: πατὴρ αὐτοῦ as subject of ἐγείραντος and ἐγερεῖ clear in both. Modality: ἐγερεῖ (future active indicative) rendered 'will raise' in both. Doctrine: repeated ἀληθῶς anti-docetic emphasis maintained; resurrection agency of Father explicit. Scripture: Philippians 2:10 allusion correctly attached to βλεπόντων clause in Pass B; 2 Corinthians 4:14 allusion correctly attached to resurrection clause in Pass B per notes. Title 'Truly born, truly crucified, truly raised' names the thought. Notes disclose OCR damage (none evident here) and uncertain readings (Lake apparatus variants on ὃς καί). Covered source paragraphs: [1]. No omissions, additions, or contradictions. All checks pass.
